files.diff_summary: Replaced DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(DateFormat.MEDIUM, DateFormat.SHORT) with new SimpleDateFormat("MMM d, yyyy h:mm a") -- the exact pattern JDK 8/JRE-COMPAT resolved for that style pair (COMPAT sample: 'Nov 14, 2023 10:13 PM'; CLDR/JDK11-default sample: 'Nov 14, 2023, 10:13 PM', which inserts a comma before the time). Declared type stays DateFormat (SimpleDateFormat extends it) -- no signature change. No import added: the file already had 'import java.text.*;', which already covers SimpleDateFormat. Empirically verified against the real jade.jar built fresh in jade-ant:11 (JDK 11): the resulting SimpleDateFormat produces the exact JDK 8/COMPAT string (no comma before the time portion), not the CLDR-default string (which inserts one). Pattern derivation: ran a probe class against jade-ant:11 with -Djava.locale.providers=COMPAT (matches JDK 8 output) and with the default provider (CLDR, the bug) for the exact style pair used at this site, for a fixed timestamp, en_US (the container's default locale).
